blind_target.title: Violent Political Rhetoric on Twitter
blind_target.evidence_quote:
To show the impact of these nonrandom removal patterns on sensitive dataset findings, I attempt to replicate central findings reported in a recent
Political Science Research and Methods
article by Kim (
Reference Kim
2023
).
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: Twitter’s policies and API dismantling hinder the replication of research studies that involve the content of tweets, especially those containing sensitive content. While there are further findings in the original paper focusing on the follower network rather than the textual content, replicating the text-related steps of the study gives an idea of the implications of nonrandom tweet removal within sensitive datasets as several groups (of words, hashtags, and political actors) are no longer equally represented in the recrawled dataset compared to the original one. This unequal representation leads to descriptive and statistical model findings that differ considerably from the published figures.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original tweet IDs are recrawled, yielding a surviving subset of the original observations, not a fresh sample. Comparable numerical output exists but differs substantively. Altering inclusion through tweet mortality removes the original gender finding.

blind_target.title: The “Out of Africa” Hypothesis, Human Genetic Diversity, and Comparative Economic Development
blind_target.evidence_quote:
We undertake a full replication guided by the econometric and data concerns raised in Guedes et al.
We follow the methods of Ashraf and Galor closely, we use improved data on heterozygosity and
population, and we identify several methodological flaws in Ashraf and Galor (2013).
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote:
Column 1 exactly replicates the Ashraf and Galor Table 1, column 1 regression, and
column 2 presents the results from the identical model but with the incorporation of the new genetic
diversity data.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote:
The last component of our analysis uncovers a coding error present in the original paper. Ashraf
and Galor fail to include the appropriate number of fixed e↵ects. When corrected, the conclusions of
their analysis regarding the mechanisms through which genetic diversity a↵ects economic development
no longer hold; according to their specifications, there seems to be no evidence that the two competing
mechanisms of the genetic diversity channel are operating simultaneously in the same set of countries.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Exact recovery of original regressions is reported. Corrected fixed effects and alternative specifications on original data challenge substantive conclusions. Expanded and updated archival data are additional extensions.

shipped.outcome_quote: We extend the analysis to include the time period 1960–2020 and more economic factors, estimate the models by farm size categories, using seemingly unrelated regression, and apply it to international settings (Brazil and the Eurozone). The role of economic factors changes according to farm size and country… Our replication of Gale (1990) does not reproduce the magnitude or statistical significance of the original estimates.

blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: The largest difference in the replication analysis is the coefficients of the ratio of nonfarm earnings to real farm income. This difference probably stems from the construction of the variable and the sources used.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Reconstructed historical data yield substantively different coefficients, including loss of significance for the price ratio. Extensions add years, farm categories and countries; these do not establish robustness on the original data alone.
